subject: Burst capacity: commit allocation, surge tiers and economic example
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated - burst add-on structure and billing mechanics

Markus,

Thanks for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and finance teams: we need clarity on three things before we can scope a PO —

1) How burst capacity is allocated across our GPU pools. If we reserve 10 GPUs as dedicated commit, and buy a burst add-on, does burst apply pool-wide or per-pool?
2) How cooldowns and surge rates are applied/charged. We often have 10–15 minute spikes; want to understand the billing for short spike events vs sustained bursts.
3) Example economics for a typical 2-week product launch: if baseline sustained traffic is 200k tokens/day and expected peak traffic is 1M tokens/day for 4 hours/day for 7 days, what does the committed + burst cost look like?

Procurement also asked about any floor/commit conversions for unused burst credits. Can you send a simple worked example and the latest pricing matrix?

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of AI Infrastructure | Acme Corp
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated - burst add-on structure and billing mechanics

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached the burst-pricing-matrix.csv and a worked-example workbook; forwarding a short runbook below so you can share with procurement. Quick answers up front:

- Allocation model: burst inventory is scoped to the Dedicated deployment, not a single GPU. That means any GPU pool (within the same dedicated instance) can draw from the burst bucket until it's exhausted. We partition at the pool level only when multiple dedicated instances exist.
- Cooldowns: the default cooldown window is 15 minutes after a surge event; subsequent surges within that window draw from the same event and are billed at the surge rate. You can request a longer cooldown (e.g., 30m) in the contract.
- Surge rates: we charge surge usage at a multiplier on top of the committed per-token rate; default multipliers are 1.35x (tier 1), 1.75x (tier 2) based on severity/guarantee.

I'm looping in Ben from Solutions so he can sketch the GPU sizing and put numbers against your launch profile.

Next steps: Ben will send a calculation and a short proposal. If procurement needs a line-item for committed-to-burst conversion (unused burst credits converting to month-of-dedicated credit), we can include that as an optional contract clause.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated - burst add-on structure and billing mechanics

Sam — hi, Ben here. I put together the quick calculation and a sizing note (see inline). Attachment: ReservedCommit_ExampleCalc.xlsx

Short technical summary:
- Baseline commit: assume you reserve 10x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) sized to deliver ~300 concurrent generation streams with 2s p95.
- Burst bucket: we sell burst as a token bucket (X tokens = Y token-hours at the committed performance profile). Burst is global across the Dedicated instance and will be consumed by any worker serving your deployment.
- Cooldown semantics: 15m (default). If you exceed the burst threshold, the system counts that as a single surge event; additional surges within 15m are treated as the same event and billed to the same surge bucket.

Worked example (numbers simplified):
- Baseline committed cost (monthly): $120k for 10 GPUs (reserved commit).
- Committed per-token rate: $0.0006/token at sustained baseline.
- Burst add-on: purchase 2M token-burst credits/month = $900 (effectively $0.00045/token if consumed).
- Surge multiplier: if you exceed burst credits, traffic is billed at 1.75x committed per-token rate until we throttle or spin additional on-demand capacity.

Two-week launch scenario (your numbers):
- Baseline usage for 14 days: 200k tokens/day * 14 = 2.8M tokens
- Peak extra usage: 4 hours/day at (1M - 200k) = 800k extra tokens/day * 7 days = 5.6M tokens
- If you buy 2M burst credits, remaining 3.6M peak tokens will be billed at surge multiplier.
- Additional cost: burst credits $900 + surge overage ~ 3.6M * ($0.0006 * 1.75) = ~$3,780 -> total extra ~ $4,680 over the period.

Notes & levers:
- If you increase burst credits to 5M/month, the example shows peak covered and avoids large surge overage.
- We can offer a committed-burst conversion: any unused burst credits at quarter-end may be converted to a credit against next-month dedicated usage at a 70% conversion rate. This is contract-level and negotiable.

I'll attach the CSV with tier examples and also propose a tiered burst-pricing:
- Tier A (pilot): 0–2M tokens @ $900/month
- Tier B (growth): 2M–10M tokens @ $0.00042/token
- Tier C (enterprise): 10M+ tokens with volume discounts and SLA-backed surge caps.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the line items.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated - burst add-on structure and billing mechanics

Thanks Ben — useful. A couple of procurement asks: 

1) Can you give us a firm cap option? Finance prefers a hard spike cap (e.g., no more than 1.3x billed for any surge beyond burst credits) rather than an open multiplier. If that means Redwood will throttle at a defined threshold, that's acceptable, we just need cost predictability.
2) For the committed-burst conversion: can you move the conversion to 85% for unused burst credits if we sign a 12-month commit? That gives us flexibility.
3) Any room for a 10–15% discount on the surge multiplier (move 1.75x -> 1.6x) if we agree to a 12-month $1.1M committed spend?

If you can send a short update to the term sheet with those options, procurement can move quickly.

—Sam
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated - burst add-on structure and billing mechanics

Sam — appreciate the clarity. We can accommodate most of this; outlines below are what I can commit to in a term-sheet addendum: 

1) Spike cap option: we will offer an Opt-In "Spike Cap" where Redwood enforces throttling beyond the defined burst+cap threshold. The billing multiplier beyond burst will be capped at 1.3x if Spike Cap is enabled. (This is operationally a throttling + cap combination.)

2) Conversion rate on unused burst credits: for a 12-month committed contract of $1.1M, we can increase unused-burst credit conversion to 85% (applies quarterly).

3) Surge multiplier discount: for the 12-month $1.1M commit we can reduce the default surge multiplier from 1.75x to 1.6x. In exchange we'll require a 45-day notice period for any material region failover and a 90-day minimum commitment window for reserved GPUs.

Additionally, commercial concessions:
- Pilot period: 3 months at 20% off burst add-on pricing to validate your launch pattern.
- Extended cooldown: we'll set the cooldown to 30 minutes as part of the pilot to reduce double-counting short repeated spikes.

I'll have legal draft the addendum and attach an updated term-sheet (term-sheet-dedicated-burst-v2.pdf). If procurement is good with the cap + conversion terms, we can circulate the DocuSign next week.

Best,
Markus
